name: Polyuse One
summary: Japanese-made, foldable gantry 3D concrete printer on casters that travels on a 4-ton truck and prints civil-works parts such as retaining walls, wave-return walls and stay-in-place formwork on or near the site.

germany.statusNote: Sold and supported in Japan only (Japanese maker, Japanese-language sales and onboarding); no German or EU distributor, CE statement or export offer found.

specs.value: three-phase 200 V 30 A or single-phase 100 V 15 A

specs.label: Transport
specs.value: folds to fit a standard 4-ton truck; caster-equipped
specs.quote: It folds down to fit on a standard 4‑ton truck, so it can be brought right up to the site.

specs.label: Onboarding
specs.conditions: support continues through the first year
specs.quote: Three days of onboarding get your team running production on its own.

specs.conditions: as of June 2026 (maker, Polyuse 3D printing overall)

specs.label: Strength of printed cores
specs.quote: Core specimens taken from printed pieces reached about 40 N/mm² or more at 28 days (under standard conditions).

notes: Gantry frame on casters; folds for transport on a 4-ton truck and is set up in about 10 minutes.
Prints with Polyuse's own premixed mortar; printed parts can serve as stay-in-place formwork for reinforced concrete.
Registered in Japan's NETIS new-technology database (KT-230174-VE).
